questions.question: Which acid destroys the bacteria that enter the stomach?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Hydrochloric acid__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hydrochloric acid is the digestive fluid formed by the stomach during the process of digestion.
 
 
• It functions by destroying harmful microorganisms present in the food particles.
 
 
 
• The digestive system of the human body comprises a group of organs that work together in converting food into energy and other basic nutrients to power the body.
 
• The stomach serves as a muscular bag that is situated towards the left side of the abdominal cavity, beneath the diaphragm.
 
 
• This vital organ acts as a storage for the food and provides enough time to digest meals.
 
• The stomach also produces digestive enzymes and hydrochloric acid that maintains the process of digestion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• Digestion and absorption are the two main functions of the digestive system.
 
 
• Digestion is necessary for breaking down food particles into nutrients that are used by the body as an energy source, cell repair and growth.
 
• Food and drink need to be converted into smaller molecules of nutrients before it is absorbed by the blood and carried to the cells throughout the body.
 
• The body breaks the nutrients present in the drinks and food into carbohydrates, vitamins, fats and proteins.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Formic acid

 
• Formic Acid is the common name of Methanoic Acid.
 
• Formic acid is the simplest carboxylic acid.
 
• Molecular Formula: HCOOH or CH2O2.
 
• Formic acid appears as a colourless liquid with a pungent odour.
 
• The word "formic" comes from the Latin word ‘formica’, meaning ant, referring to its early isolation by the distillation of ant bodies.
 
• In nature, formic acid is found in most ants and in stingless bees.

Sulfuric acid

 
• Sulphuric acid is an oily liquid that is viscous in nature. 
 
• Sulphuric acid is highly acidic.
 
• The chemical formula of this compound is H2SO4.
 
• it is used in the manufacture of batteries, detergents like trisodium phosphate, potato farming, printing ink, as a dehydrating agent, making paper, perfume, disinfectants, drugs etc.

Nitric acid

 
• Nitric Acid is a strong acid with the chemical formula HNO3.
 
• It is also known as the spirit of niter and aqua fortis.
 
• In its pure form, it is colourless but as it gets older it turns into a yellow cast.
 
• This colour appears due to the decomposition of Nitric acid to oxides of nitrogen and water.
 
• It is highly corrosive and toxic.
 
• It causes severe skin burns.
 
• It can be manufactured by the catalytic oxidation of ammonia.
 
• It is a common reagent used in laboratories and an important chemical used in industries to manufacture explosives and fertilizers.
 
• The** pH** of Nitric acid is approximately 3.01.

questions.question: Which among the following wind is associated with extreme cold and dryness?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Polar Easterlies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Polar easterlies are dry, cold prevailing winds that blow from the east.
 
• They emanate from the polar highs, areas of high pressure around the North and South Poles.
 
• Polar easterlies flow to low-pressure areas in sub-polar regions.
 
• Westerlies are prevailing winds that blow from the west at mid-latitudes.
 
• These winds are also called trades winds because winds blow from subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equatorial low-pressure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Seasonal winds

 
 
• The winds which change their direction in different seasons.
 
• For example, the monsoons in India are seasonal winds. 
 
 
 
• Local winds
 
 
• This wind flow are caused by the uneven heat of the Earth's surface within a small area.
 
• Local winds form only when strong winds are weak.

questions.question:
Cash reserve ratio is a ________ tool to control money supply.

I. Qualitative

II. Quantitative
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Monetary policy tools are of two types - 

 
• Quantitative Monetary policy tools
 
• Qualitative Monetary policy tools

 

Quantitative instruments influence the money volume and credit supply in the system.

The quantitative instruments are Open Market Operations, Liquidity Adjustment Facility (Repo and Reverse Repo), Marginal Standing Facility, SLR, CRR, Bank Rate, etc.

Open Market Operations:

__
 
• Open market operations (OMO) refers to the buying and selling of government securities in the open market in order to expand or contract the amount of money in the banking system, facilitated by the Federal Reserve.
 
• Open Market Operations are carried out in Gilt Edged Market.

Cash Reserve Ratio:

 
• The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) refers to the share of Net Demand and Time Liabilities that banks have to hold as balances with the RBI.
 
• The objective of CRR is to keep inflation under control.
 
• During high inflation in the economy, the central bank raises the CRR to lower the bank’s loanable funds.

Bank Rate: 

 
• The RBI can influence money supply by changing the rate at which it gives loans to the commercial banks. This rate is called the Bank Rate in India.
 
• By increasing the bank rate, loans taken by commercial banks become more expensive; this reduces the reserves held by the commercial bank and hence decreases the money supply. A fall in the bank rate can increase the money supply.

Margin Requirments:

 
• Margin requirement refers to the difference between the current value of the security offered for loan (called collateral) and the value of loan granted.
 
• It is a qualitative method of credit control adopted by the central bank in order to stabilize the economy from inflation or deflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Qualitative Monetary tools used in monetary policy regulation are as follows:

 
• Fixing Margin Requirements: The margin refers to the “proportion of the loan amount which is not financed by the bank”. Or in other words, it is that part of a loan which a borrower has to raise in order to get finance for his purpose. A change in a margin implies a change in the loan size.
 
• Consumer Credit Regulation: Under this method, the consumer credit supply is regulated through the hire-purchase and installment sale of consumer goods. This can help in checking the credit use and then inflation in a country.
 
• Publicity: This is yet another method of selective credit control. Through it, Central Bank (RBI) publishes various reports stating what is good and what is bad in the system. This published information can help commercial banks to direct credit supply in the desired sectors.
 
• Credit Rationing: Central Bank fixes the credit amount to be granted. Credit is rationed by limiting the amount available for each commercial bank. This method controls even bill re-discounting. For certain purposes, the upper limit of credit can be fixed and banks are told to stick to this limit. This can help in lowering banks' credit exposure to unwanted sectors.
 
• Moral Suasion: It implies to pressure exerted by the RBI on the Indian banking system without any strict action for compliance with the rules. It is a suggestion to banks. It helps in restraining credit during inflationary periods. Under moral suasion, central banks can issue directives, guidelines, and suggestions for commercial banks regarding reducing credit supply for speculative purposes.
 
• Control Through Directives: Under this method the central bank issue frequent directives to commercial banks. These directives guide commercial banks in framing their lending policy. Through a directive, the central bank can influence credit structures, the supply of credit to certain limits for a specific purpose. The RBI issues directives to commercial banks for not lending loans to the speculative sectors such as securities, etc beyond a certain limit.
 
• Direct Action: Under this method, the RBI can impose action against a bank. If certain banks are not adhering to the RBI’s directives, the RBI may refuse to re-discount their bills and securities.

questions.question: According to census 2011, which Union territory has highest decadal population growth rate between 2001-11?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadra & Nagar Haveli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli recorded the highest decadal population growth rate between 2001-2011, according to Census 2011.
 
• The population of Dadra and Nagar Haveli increased from approximately **220,490 in 2001 to 343,709 in 2011,** a growth rate of **55.88%**.
 
• This is the highest growth rate among the Union Territories during this period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other main points of the Census 2011:
 
 
• In comparison to **15 States/UTs** with a share of roughly 42% during the period 1991-2001, where **25 States/UTs** with a share of nearly** 85%** of the nation's population had an** annual growth rate of less than 2%.**
 
• **Between 2001 and 2011, **15 States/UTs experienced annual growth rates of less than** 1.5%,** compared to just 4 in the prior decade.
 
• There are **158.8 million kids **in the **0 to 6 age range** overall (5 million since 2001).
 
• Over a million kids between the** ages of 0 and 6 **are presently present in **twenty States and Union Territories.**
 
• The **sex ratio** has decreased in three important States** (J&K, Bihar, and Gujarat)** when compared to **Census 2001.**
 
• **Kerala with 1084 **has the **highest sex ratio **followed by **Puducherry with 1038, and Daman & Diu **has the **lowest sex ratio of 618.**
 
• **Mizoram** has the** highest child sex ratio (0-6 years) **of **971** followed by **Meghalaya with 970.**
 
• **Punjab** comes in second with a** ratio of 846** while **Haryana **is last with a **ratio of 830.**
 
• The **literacy rate** increased by **9.21 percentage points** from** 64.83 per cent **in 2001 to** 74.04** per cent in 2011.
 
• The percentage increase in literacy between 2001 and 2011 is 38.82; for** men, it is 31.98% and for women, it is 49.10%.**
 
• The population is aged seven and older are made up of **74% literate people and 26% illiterate people.**

questions.question: Which among the following countries will host the 2024 South Asian Games?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The 2024 South Asian Games will be hosted by** Pakistan**.
 
• The games will be held in **Lahore, the capital of Punjab province**.
 
• The games were originally scheduled to be held in **March 2023**, but were later postponed to March 2024 by the **South Asia Olympic Council (SAOC) **members at the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) conference in** Phnom Penh, Cambodia**.
 
• Pakistan has hosted the South Asian Games twice before, in **1989 and 2004**.
 
• Both times, the games were held in **Islamabad**.
 
• The South Asian Games is a quadrennial multi-sport event that is held among **athletes from South Asia**.
 
• The governing body of these games is the SAOC, which is formed by 7 member countries:** Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka**.

• The games are expected to attract over** 5,000 athletes from 7 member countries**.

questions.question: The Inter-State Council consists of ________ ministers of Cabinet rank in the Union Council of Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Inter-State-Council was set up under Article 263 of the Constitution of India vide Presidential Order dated 28.5.1990.
 
• Inter-State Council is a recommendatory body with duties to investigate and discuss the subjects of common interest between the Union and State(s). 
 
• The inter-state council is Chaired by the Prime Minister. 
 
• The present composition of the Council is as follows: 
 
 
• Prime Minister(Chairman)
 
• Chief Ministers of all States
 
• Chief Ministers of Union Territories having a Legislative Assembly and Administrators of UTs not having a Legislative Assembly and
 
• Governors of States under President’s Rule(Governor’s Rule in the case of J&K)
 
• **Six Ministers** of Cabinet rank in the Union Council of Ministers to be nominated by the Prime Minister.
 
• Four Ministers of Cabinet rank as Permanent invitees Members. 
 
 

Note:- Other Ministers and Ministers of State having independent charge in the Union Government may be invited as permanent invitees if so nominated by the Chairman of the Council, or as and when any item relating to a subject under their charge is to be discussed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The Union Government constituted a Commission in 1983 under the Chairmanship of Justice R.S. Sarkaria to review the working of the existing arrangements between the Union and the States.
 
• ​One of the important recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission was for establishing a permanent Inter-State Council as an independent national forum for consultation with a mandate well defined in accordance with Article 263 of the Constitution of India.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution by the ________ Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental duties were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
 
• The committee suggested that the duty to pay taxes to be included in the fundamental duties
 
• The committee also recommended that the legislatures should prescribe law for imposing a penalty for violation of the duties.
 
 
• But paying taxes and penalty for violation duties are not incorporated in the constitution.
 
 
 
• Statement 3 is also not recommended by the committee because as per the recommendation the law made by legislatures to impose a penalty shall not be questioned in the court on the ground of infringement of any of fundamental rights. ​__
 
 

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Article
 Explanation
 
 
 
 

 Article 35
 This article gives the power to Parliament to determine the acts and laws that will govern who can be a citizen of India. It is divided into two parts - Article 35(a) and Article 35(b). It also empowers the parliament to limit or abrogate the fundamental rights of the armed forces, para-military forces, police forces, intelligence agencies and similar services where the maintenance of discipline is deemed to be of paramount importance.
 
 

 Article 47
 Article 47 falls under the directive principles of state policy. It states that the State has a duty to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health. The State shall regard the raising of the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties and, in particular, the State shall endeavour to bring about prohibition of the consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health.
 
 

 Article 51
 This article is also part of the directive principles of state policy. It mandates that the State shall endeavor to: promote international peace and security, maintain just and honorable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

questions.question: "Mission Karmayogi" programme is for ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Civil servants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National Civil Service Capacity Building Program (NPCSCB) is known as Mission Karmayogi.
 
• The Indian bureaucracy has undergone a transformation. On September 2, 2020, the Union Cabinet officially unveiled it.
 
• The mission's goal is to provide the groundwork for the capacity building of Indian public employees and to improve governance in the country.
 
• The Union Cabinet has started Mission Karmayogi. Between 2020 and 2025, it intends to construct a new national architecture for civil service capacity building at the person, institutional, and process levels.
 
• To carry out this aim, the Companies Act 2013 establishes a special purpose vehicle (SPV) (a non-profit corporation).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) aspires to produce a professional, well-trained, and forward-looking civil service that is imbued with a shared awareness of India's developmental goals, national programs, and objectives.
 
• The NPCSCB's main goal is to improve citizen-government interaction and make it easier to live and do business. This requires civil servants to develop both functional and behavioral competencies.
 
• The time from 2014 to 2019 was used to achieve the development pre-requisites, and the next five years will be used to meet the aspirations. Mission Karmayogi is part of a longer-term reform movement in public HRM and governance that began in 2015.

questions.question: In 1895, Mahatma Gandhi, along with other Indians has established ________ to fight against racial discrimination.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Natal Congress**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Natal Indian Congress was an organization that aimed to fight discrimination against Indians in South Africa.
 
• The Natal Indian Congress was founded by Mahatma Gandhi along with other Indians in 1895.
 
• Gandhi was the Honorary Secretary and Abdoola Hajee Adam Jhaveri (Dada Abdulla) was elected president.
 
• The Natal Congress in its early stages focused on providing equality to all races and people of all castes, genders, and Creeds.
 
• From the 1920s the organization functioned under the umbrella organization, the SAIC (South African Indian Congress).
 
• However, in the 1930s-1940s, the NIC experienced more radical leadership when Dr. G.M. Naicker emerged on the scene.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Name
 Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Dev Samaj
 Religious/Social Organization
 Dev Samaj is a socio-religious organization established in 1887 by Bhagwan Dev Atma in Lahore. It promotes ethical, moral, and social values among people. It runs several educational institutions in Punjab and Haryana, emphasizing moral and value-based education.
 
 

 Brahmo Samaj
 Religious/Social Reform Movement
 Brahmo Samaj is a socio-religious reform movement in India that was founded in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. The Brahmo Samaj movement played a significant role in the reformation of Indian society during the 19th century. It denounced idol worship and the caste system and advocated for equal rights for women, including education and the right to inheritance and property.
 
 

 Sabarmati Ashram
 Historic Site and Monument
 Sabarmati Ashram, also known as Gandhi Ashram, is located in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India, on the banks of the Sabarmati River. It was one of the residences of Mahatma Gandhi, who lived there for about 12 years during India's freedom struggle. It was from here that Gandhi initiated the famous Dandi March in 1930. Today, it serves as a monument to Gandhi's life and works and contains a museum with several of his personal items.

questions.question: Fern is an example of which plant group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pteridophyta **is a division of the **plant kingdom that includes ferns and their allies.**
 
• **Ferns are characterized by their large, divided leaves.**
 
• **They reproduce via spores, not seeds, and do not produce flowers or fruit.**
 
• They are vascular plants, meaning they have specialized tissues, **xylem and phloem, for transporting water and nutrients.**
 
• **Pteridophytes are predominantly found in damp, shady places, although some are adapted to dry environments.**
 
• Ferns are the most diverse group within the** Pteridophyta, with over 10,000 species worldwide.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 

 Phanerogams
 
 
 
• These are seed-producing plants and are also called Spermatophytes.
 
• Phanerogams are further divided into gymnosperms (non-flowering plants that produce cones and seeds) and angiosperms (flowering plants, seeds enclosed within an ovary).
 
 
 
 

 Bryophyta
 
 
 
• This group comprises the mosses, hornworts, and liverworts.
 
• They are non-vascular plants, i.e., they do not have specialized tissues for the transport of water and nutrients.
 
• Bryophytes are usually found in damp environments.
 
 
 
 

 Thallophyta
 
 
 
• This is an older classification and it traditionally includes a wide array of organisms like algae, fungi, and lichens, which have a thallus-like (undifferentiated) structure.
 
• This grouping is generally not used in modern taxonomical classification.

questions.question: Hindustan Aeronautics limited comes under which sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) **is an Indian state-owned **aerospace and defence company headquartered in Bangalore, India.**
 
• It is governed under the **management of the Indian Ministry of Defence.**
 
• The **public sector consists of organizations and institutions owned and operated by the government.**
 
• They provide services to the public, and the revenue comes from the government treasury.
 
• **HAL **is involved in the **operations of the aerospace industry, including the manufacturing and assembly of aircraft, navigation, and related communication equipment, as well as operating airports.**
 
• It provides these services to the **Indian Armed Forces predominantly and has a significant role in the defense sector of the country.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Sector
 Explanation
 
 
 
 

 Co-operative Sector
 
 
 
• This sector includes organizations run by the people themselves for mutual benefit.
 
• They aren't owned by the state and their aim is to serve the interests of their members rather than to earn profits.
 
• Examples include credit unions, cooperative housing, and farmers' co-ops.
 
 
 
 

 Private Sector
 
 
 
• The private sector consists of organizations and institutions that are not controlled by the government.
 
• These organizations are run by individuals or companies with the aim of making a profit.
 
• Examples include private companies like Tata Motors, Reliance Industries, and Infosys.
 
 
 
 

 Foreign Sector
 
 
 
• The foreign sector is made up of businesses and industries from other countries operating in different countries.
 
• These can include multinational corporations, international organizations, and foreign governments.
 
• Examples would be companies like Microsoft, Toyota, and Nestle operating in India.

questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of Inertia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Law of Inertia, **Newton's first law of motion, states that an object at rest tends to stay at rest, and an object in motion tends to stay in motion unless acted upon by an external force.**
 
• The term **'inertia' refers to the resistance of an object to change its state of motion.**
 
• It can be thought of as a property of mass to resist change.
 
• If an object is at rest,** it will remain at rest unless an unbalanced force acts upon it.**
 
• If an object is in motion**, it will continue to move in a straight line at a constant speed unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.**
 
• This law introduces the concept of a frame of reference.
 
• The descriptions of motion** depend on the observer, and different observers may observe different states of motion.**
 
• An important consequence of this law is the** idea of conservation of momentum.**
 
• If the net force on an object is zero,** its momentum (mass times velocity) remains constant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion include three fundamental principles:**
 
• **Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia):**
 
 
• **​**An object will remain at** rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.**
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law:**
 
 
• **​**The rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the force applied.
 
• It is typically formulated as ***F=ma*, where F is the force applied, m is the mass of the object, and a is the acceleration produced.**
 
 
 
• **Newton's Third Law:**
 
 
• **​**For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• It means that any force exerted on a **body will create a force of equal magnitude but in the opposite direction on the object which exerted the first force.**
